title: SLO playground probe notes — crossfunctional ops
body:
Purpose and framing:
This doc captures a short experimental plan for a ‘SLO playground’ — a lightweight, cross-functional probe to validate SLO onboarding patterns for new model-serving routes. Goal is to run 2–3 quick experiments across product, platform, and SRE to identify friction, measure signal fidelity, and produce a tiny runbook we can iterate on.

High level hypothesis:
- If we provide a minimal SLO onboarding checklist + prebuilt dashboards and a 2-week canary cadence, teams will successfully declare, measure, and act on SLOs with <2x ramp time vs. current ad-hoc process.
- We expect to find 3 categories of friction: metric mapping, alert noise tuning, and traffic routing for fallbacks.

Scope (what we will do in this probe):
- Select 2 serving routes (1 chat endpoint, 1 embedding pipeline) that are low-to-medium risk.
- Ship a minimal SLO definition, dashboard, alert rules, and a 2-week canary rollout.
- Capture time-to-first-SLO, triage events, false positive alerts, and required config changes.
- Run 2 post-canary retros and publish a 1-page onboarding runbook.

SLO definitions (starter templates) — to be tuned per route:
- Availability SLO: 99.95% measured as successful 2xx responses over rolling 30d (target: 99.95, burn rate thresholds: 4h at 10% burn triggers comms).
- Latency SLO (chat): p95 < 180ms for inference-only path (objective) and p95 < 300ms for end-to-end request (including proxy).
- Error budget guardrail (embeddings): error-rate <0.5% (model inference errors + 5xx).
Notes: these are intentionally permissive for the probe; production targets may tighten.

Experiment timeline (4 weeks total):
- Week 0 (prep, 3 days): stakeholder kickoff, route selection, metric plumbing check (observability owner: Noah).
- Week 1 (canary start): apply SLO definitions, create dashboards, enable alerting (owner: Priya/Ethan).
- Week 2 (canary observe): monitor, tune thresholds, record incidents or noisy alerts. Daily 15-min stand.
- Week 3 (ramp/rollback test): simulate degraded nodes / injected latency, observe fallback behavior, validate rollback.
- Week 4 (retro + runbook): capture findings, publish 1-pager, list action items for platform integration.

Runbook skeleton (for the two routes) — keeps it short and actionable:
- Title: <route> — quick recovery play
- Symptoms: observed p95 > target for >15m OR error budget burn > threshold
- Immediate checks (5m): recent deploy? config drift? model variant fallback active?
- Quick mitigations (10–30m): switch traffic to fallback model; increase autoscaler min replicas; reduce batch size for latency-sensitive path. Steps include exact CLI/Console steps with links.
- Escalation: page SRE-oncall -> include runbook link, recent dashboard snapshot, request id list.

Measurement plan (what success looks like):
- Primary metrics: time-to-declare SLO (hours), time-to-first-stable-alert (days), number of false-positive alerts during probe, and mean time-to-lower-burn (MTTLB) during induced incidents.
- Targets: declare SLO within 48h of route selection; first usable dashboard within 72h; <=3 noisy alerts in 2-week canary.

Tooling & dashboards (practical notes):
- Use prebuilt dashboard template: SLO-playground-v1 in observability (dashboard id: obs-678).
- Required queries (examples to copy/paste):
  - availability: sum(success_count) / sum(total_count) by route over 30d.
  - p95 latency: histogram_quantile(0.95, rate(inference_latency_bucket[5m])) by route.
  - error budget: 1 - availability over rolling window.
- Ownership map: Noah (metrics plumbing), Ava (dashboards + alerts), Ethan (canary automation), Priya (runbook + retro).

Risk matrix (quick):
- High likelihood, low impact: alert noise. Mitigation: initially suppress non-ES signals and tune alert windows.
- Low likelihood, high impact: fallback model incompatible with route. Mitigation: pre-validate fallback in staging.

Open questions / TODOs (notes to self):
- Can we programmatically derive candidate SLO targets from historical traffic? (CONF-1423 mentions some heuristics).
- Do product teams accept our p95 latency calculation (proxy vs inference-only)? Need product alignment call. -> Action: schedule 30m with Console PM (Sofia) in next 3 days.
- What telemetry is missing on the embedding pipeline for proper error classification? Ticket SRE-231 created.

Meeting checklist for kickoff:
- Quick intro (5m), scope and routes (10m), tools and owner confirmation (10m), success metrics and retro cadence (5m).
- Slack channel: #slo-playground-experiments (create after kickoff).

Post-mortem & retro template (for probe end):
- What went well
- Biggest sources of friction
- Concrete action items (owner + ETA)
- Changes to platform templates + followups (prio A/B/C)

Immediate next steps (this week):
1) Confirm route candidates — Noah to post route list by 2026-03-08.
2) Validate metric plumbing for both routes — Noah + Ethan by 2026-03-10.
3) Create dashboard template copy and share — Ava by 2026-03-11.
4) Book 30m alignment with Console PM Sofia — Priya by 2026-03-06.

Quick notes to self (informal):
- Keep runbook language super explicit (CLI commands + console clicks). Teams skip ambiguous steps and that causes delays.
- For the probe, avoid mission-critical routes — this is about process validation not SLAs.
- Save examples of noisy alerts to include in onboarding doc — helps teams understand tuning.

Appendix (links & snippets):
- Example alert rule (pseudo):
  alert: SLOBurnHigh
  expr: (1 - (sum(success_count) / sum(total_count))) > 0.005 for 15m
  labels: team=serving, severity=page
- Quick PR to copy for dashboards: github.com/redwood/reliability/pull/482 (dashboard template + queries)

End of doc — keep short, iterate.
